GLOBAL URGENT ALERT

— CONFIRMED NEWS: The long-awaited revelation of Pfizer's secret and highly classified list of side effects for the COVID-19 vaccine

— And the reality is worse than you imagined! They tried to hide this from you!

The disclosure of information on October 9, 2026, brought Pfizer's long-suppressed list of adverse effects before the public eye.

Pharmaceutical companies and their allied media spent four years downplaying concerns; skeptics were branded as "conspiracy theorists" and "science deniers."

This update draws from Pfizer's own compilation of reported side effects—data that was withheld even as the public was assured harms were rare and mild.

The list goes far beyond fever or fatigue; it is a record of serious, deadly, and life-altering health conditions acknowledged by the company itself.

Blood clotting cases include clots that can lead to stroke, heart attack, or pulmonary embolism, plus deep vein thrombosis, hepatic and spinal artery thrombosis, innominate vein thrombosis, and ventricular mural thrombi. Brainstem embolism and thrombosis are also listed as blockages that can result in loss of motor function, breathing, and death.

Hundreds of cardiac arrest cases were recorded; terms like heart failure, cardiogenic shock, myocarditis, and pericarditis describe conditions where the heart becomes inflamed, weakened, or stops working. "Sudden death" is explicitly mentioned.

Neurological cases are no less severe; the list includes acute flaccid myelitis (paralysis resembling polio), hemorrhagic encephalitis and brainstem encephalitis, central nervous system vasculitis, frontal and temporal lobe epilepsy, generalized tonic-clonic seizures, neonatal seizures, epileptic psychosis, facial paralysis, and Hashimoto's encephalopathy. Conditions like acute kidney injury, autoimmune hepatitis, liver damage, pancreatitis, interstitial lung disease, and shingles reactivation can lead to dialysis, scarring, or organ failure. The list also includes multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children and newly onset type 1 diabetes.

Mandatory measures did not spare fertility and infant issues; cases of anti-sperm antibodies and autoimmune orchitis point to immune attacks that may impair male fertility. Cases of fetal distress, low birth weight, stillbirth, neonatal death, and neonatal vein thrombosis describe harms to the fetus and newborn.

This data was known, even as refusal was viewed as betrayal.

That is the charge for October 2026; they knew, they hid the true scope of the matter, and yet they imposed the product on workers, service members, and parents.

Voices close to Trump and others from the Kennedy era at the Department of Health and Human Services had warned that these facts were being buried. Now, with the truth exposed, accountability emerges as the priority.

📊 Visa finds 46% in Asia Pacific may use stablecoins by 2031 

📣 Stablecoin interest has moved well ahead of actual use across Asia Pacific, with 46% of surveyed consumers saying they are likely to use the tokens within five years compared with 16% who used them during the past year. The research found strong interest in using stablecoins for online purchases, travel, overseas shopping and moving money across borders. Yet the survey showed a large knowledge gap, with only 6% of respondents demonstrating what Visa described as an accurate understanding of how stablecoins work.

⭐️ Across the 14 markets, 46% of respondents said they were likely to use stablecoins during the next five years. Only 16% reported using them during the previous 12 months. Visa did not disclose in its release what those existing users had used stablecoins for. The 16% figure could therefore include trading, transfers, payments or other cryptocurrency activity and should not be treated solely as consumer payment adoption.

‼️ Cross-border transfers produced one of the strongest future-use readings. Around 49% of respondents said they thought stablecoins could become a common method of moving money between countries within five years. Visa Head of Digital Currencies for Asia Pacific Nischint Sanghavi said consumers were starting to consider stablecoins for “online purchases, travel and cross-border transfers.” The company views those uses as potential extensions of existing payment behavior.

Crypto Idea

Following up on the previous post about US Treasuries.

It’s quite symbolic that The Economist recently featured a cover asking “Will Bonds Blow Up?” and warning of an impending sovereign debt crisis.

There are growing concerns that it’s becoming increasingly expensive for the US to borrow money. Investors are demanding higher and higher yields amid massive debt, budget deficits, and inflation risks. But there’s an interesting paradox here. While we’re focused on the US, the debt problem could blow up much sooner somewhere else entirely.

Take France, for example. It’s the second-largest economy in the European Union. Its public debt is approaching 120% of GDP this year, the budget deficit is around 5.4%, and 10-year bond yields have nearly reached 5%, their highest levels since 2002. For comparison, when Greece’s sovereign debt crisis began in 2009, its debt stood at around 127% of GDP. To be fair, its budget deficit was much worse, exceeding 15%. So France today is certainly not Greece in 2009, but some of the numbers are starting to look uncomfortably familiar.

And this is where things get really interesting. If France’s problems turn into a full-blown debt crisis, we’re no longer talking about a small country on the periphery of Europe. France accounts for nearly 16% of the EU’s entire economy. A crisis of that scale would almost certainly push investors to look for the safest and most liquid places to park their capital.

Some money is already flowing out of French bonds and into German bonds, the Swiss franc, and the US dollar. If the situation becomes truly systemic, US Treasuries could once again become an obvious destination. Demand for them would rise, bond prices would go up, yields would fall, and suddenly it would become cheaper for America to borrow.

And that’s the key takeaway. There are no perfect assets and no perfect countries in the markets. Capital always goes where it sees the best available alternative. That’s why a scenario in which Europe experiences a debt crisis before the US could actually turn the dollar and US Treasuries into beneficiaries of the very crisis that everyone in America is so worried about right now. For investors, that’s yet another reason not to bet everything on a single scenario and to keep a close eye not just on the US, but also on what’s happening with European debt.
